claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi can be a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
The proposed initial alloy is homogeneous, well annealed, has a uniform grain structure, and contains minimal intergranular precipitates.
Toughness degradation in an initially single-phase HEA arises from a stress- and temperature-induced grain-boundary complexion transition.
Subtle local compositional fluctuations enhanced by trace impurities trigger the proposed complexion transition.
Trace oxygen and nitrogen can promote chemical or phase segregation during aging at 700°C.
Trace impurities or local chemical fluctuations enrich specifically at grain boundaries under high-temperature and high-strain conditions.
The grain boundary changes from a ductile, disordered state to an ordered, impurity-segregated complexion that behaves as a brittle intergranular film.
The proposed complexion transition reduces grain-boundary cohesive strength without forming large intermetallic precipitates.
Reduced grain-boundary cohesion initiates and facilitates intergranular crack propagation, producing brittle behavior.
A precipitation-strengthened HEA can exhibit an elevated-temperature ductility drop associated with intergranular fracture.
Grain-boundary morphology can strongly affect elevated-temperature tensile fracture strain and creep rupture life in a precipitation-strengthened HEA.
Specimens with added impurities or induced complexion transitions will have lower fracture toughness and earlier grain-boundary crack initiation than ultra-high-purity controls.
Conventional-alloy toughness loss is driven predominantly by coarse, brittle grain-boundary intermetallic precipitates.
Temperatures of 650–700°C are relevant conditions for studying elevated-temperature degradation in HEAs.
The proposed mechanism should dominate under high-temperature, high-stress service conditions.
The proposed mechanism should become less relevant under low-temperature or minimal-loading conditions.
A comparison of otherwise identical ultra-high-purity and impurity-added specimens under identical aging and loading provides a controlled test of the mechanism.
If the two batches show neither a significant grain-boundary composition or structure difference nor a toughness difference, the proposed impurity-mediated complexion mechanism is falsified.
